split.rule: validation / training MSE of the shipped model at random_state 42 must exceed the same ratio at random_state 0 and 7: a model predicts the rows it was trained on better than the rest

selection_note: Computed once on the whole experiment, as the notebook does; the selection does not apply.

design.class_1_rule: p > 2 GeV (fewer than 50 validation rows lie above 10 GeV)
design.sampler: pandas pool.sample(min(n, len(pool)), random_state=42) per class, then concat and sample(frac=1, random_state=42), as the notebook
design.prediction: the shipped regressor's momentum, thresholded at 2 GeV

confusion.layout: rows: true class 0, 1; columns: predicted class 0, 1

interval.label: 95 % percentile bootstrap over the 47 rows (B = 2,000, seed 42)

parity.label: The notebook's metrics, for parity: accuracy, balanced accuracy, and precision, recall and F1 weighted by class support (zero_division = 0). Point values from sklearn, without intervals.

minority.note: The minority class has 20 rows: every rate whose denominator is that class rests on that many events, and its Wilson interval is correspondingly wide.

notes.intervals: Each rate carries a 95 % Wilson score interval of a proportion; the balanced accuracy, a mean of two rates, a seeded percentile bootstrap over the sample's rows, drawn as the multinomial of the four confusion counts - the same distribution as resampling the rows.
notes.counts: The confusion matrix is counts, which carry no interval.
notes.weighted: Support-weighted precision, recall and F1 are dominated by the majority class at 99 : 1; they are the notebook's numbers, kept for parity, and the per-class rates are what the card draws.
